en.question: A company has built the same Jira integration three times — once each for Claude Code, an internal chat app, and a CI bot. What does MCP offer here?

options.text: One server implementing the integration once, reusable by every client.
Faster execution of the tool calls that reach the Jira instance itself.
options.note: MCP standardises the interface; it is not a performance optimisation.

options.text: Authentication handled by the protocol, removing per-client configuration.
options.note: Authentication still has to be configured; MCP defines the protocol only.

options.text: A reduced per-token rate applied to requests that invoke MCP tools.
options.note: Token pricing is unaffected by how tools are exposed.

en.explanation: This is precisely the duplication MCP exists to remove: implement once against an open standard, and any compatible client can consume it, leaving one codebase to maintain and secure.
